- **Oil Prices Rise but Remain Unimpressed from Recent Re-Escalation –** Brent crude oil prices have **steadily risen into the mid/high-$90s** range, though volatility has compressed relative to the extreme spikes observed earlier in the conflict. While **calculating exact volumes transiting the Strait of Hormuz remains difficult** due to opaque "dark" shipping activity, current assessments indicate that global oil flows remain structurally lower than pre-war baselines. The upward pressure on prices has been primarily constrained by **subdued demand from China**, something that most analyst believe is transitory. Yet, looking toward 2027 and beyond, the core risk for energy markets rests on demand trajectories; **actual demand destruction** remains difficult to quantify, and structural shifts, evidenced by surging Chinese electric vehicle (EV) sales, point to an **accelerated adoption of alternative** transport technologies that could permanently lower global oil demand projections.
- **Our Long-term View –** The tanker market has been recovering from a long period of staggered rates as the growth in new vessel supply shrunk while oil demand remained elevated in line with the global economy. The recent rapid increase in freight rates has led to significant new vessel ordering, with the orderbook now standing at well above average levels, and although in the near term such a supply/demand misbalance is small, we expect a meaningful negative balance to develop longer term leading to an industry downcycle.

Happy New Year!
Following the start of the year, we see continuous activity on both dry and tanker markets.
The dry cargo market has held up with a steady flow of transactions, while the tanker sector has seen particularly strong momentum, driven by significant VLCC deals that have set a confident tone for the opening weeks of the year.
Dry Cargo
In the larger segment, we are hearing rumors of a 2011 Japanese built Capesize being committed at levels of USD 32.5 m net, while at the Kamsarmax front, the CENTURY SHANGHAI (ABT 81K DWT, 2018, CHENGXI) has been sold via auction for USD 25.02 m.
In the Ultramax segment, the STARRY NIGHT (ABT 61K DWT, 2022, NANTONG COSCO) achieved a price of USD 32.5 m, basis March - April delivery.
Furthermore, another auction sale has been concluded, with the Supramax JIANG YUAN NAN JING (ABT 50K DWT, 2003, NACKS) achieving levels of USD 7.54 m.
In the Handysize sector, the FETHIYE-M (ABT 37K DWT, 2011, SPP GOSEONG) has now been sold to Greek interests in the high USD 12 m, while the BULKER BEE 30 (ABT 34K DWT, 2010, TK) has been sold at USD 11.3 m. Finally, we are hearing of a 2016 Tsuneishi Cebu built Handysize being committed for levels of USD 19.1 m.
Tanker
The key transaction of the week involved c/o Frontline selling 8 x VLCCs (2015-2016 built - 1st generation ECO m/e) for an aggregate value of USD 831.5 m, with deliveries scheduled during Q1 2026. In parallel, the owners have agreed to acquire 9 x Newbuilding VLCCs with scrubbers for the amount of USD 1.224 bn, with deliveries running from Q3 2026 throughout Q2 2027.
In addition, c/o CMB.TECH have sold 6 x VLCCs (2007-2016 built) enbloc, with deliveries also scheduled for Q1 202

After the significant S&P activity observed last week, especially driven by the VLCC segment,the wet market remains highly active, with substantial movement observed across all segments.
On the dry side, although there has been some softening on rates, S&P demand remains present and acquisitions continue to emerge, with buyers adopting a cautious but opportunistic approach.
Dry Cargo
This week, dry bulk activity was concentrated in the larger segments, where c/o Berge Bulk sold their scrubber-fitted Newcastlemax BERGE MOLDOVEANU (ABT 211K DWT, 2020, BOHAI, SCRUBBER), for a price in the region of USD 74 m to Korean interests.
Furthermore, we are hearing of two Capesize units being sold this week, the FRONTIER KOTOBUKI (174K DWT, 2011, NAMURA) which was inviting offers yesterday, we understand that has been committed for USD 31 m, and another vintage unit which is built in Japan 2005 at a price of USD 20.5 m.
In the geared segment, the Ultramax OCEAN JASMIN (ABT 63K DWT, 2019, COSCO HI ZHOUSHAN) has been sold in the region of USD 28.5 m basis TC attached until max June 2026.
Unconfirmed rumors suggest two Ultramax transactions being concluded, including a 2012 Japanese built unit at a price in the low USD 19 m and a 2020 Chinese built vessel, said to be sold for xs USD 30 m.
On the smaller segment, c/o Straits Orient Lines sold their Handysize TBC PRAISE (ABT 36K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI MIPO) for USD 14.4 m, while on the Chinese built front, we understand that a 37K DWT, 2012 unit is being negotiated in the levels of low/mid USD 11 m.
Tanker
The tanker sector has remained busy, VLCC transactions continued to unfold, while demand remains notably strong throughout different sizes, reflecting sustained buyer interest and confident sentiment.

Another active week on the tanker front, with a steady flow of transactions and ongoing negotiationstaking place across all vessel segments.
On the dry side, interest remains high with several new sales emerging as market sentiment strengthens.
Dry Cargo
On the Kamsarmax front, the MIAO XIANG (ABT 81K DWT, 2013, JIANGSU EASTERN) has been sold at USD 16.8 m, while on the Panamax segment, the KT BIRDIE (ABT 74K DWT, 2011, SASEBO HI) changed hands at USD 16.5 m to Greek interests.
We are also hearing that a 2020 Chinese built Ultramax has been sold for USD 30.1 m. Meanwhile, THE LOVING (ABT 58K DWT, 2007, TSUNEISHI CEBU) has been committed at USD 11.7 m.
On the Handysize segment, we are seeing several transactions unfolding and negotiations taking place, highlighting also buyers' appetite for smaller tonnage. The YANGTZE GRACE & YANGTZE HAPPINESS (ABT 32K DWT, 2012, JIANGMEN NANYANG) were sold for USD 9.8 m each to separate Chinese interests. According to market rumors a 37K DWT 2008 Japanese built Handysize has been sold for USD 11.4 m, whilst a 2015 Japanese built 36K DWT Handysize is in firm discussions in the high USD 18's m.
Tanker
On the Suezmax segment, c/o Okeanis have agreed to acquire two resale Suezmaxes currently under construction at Daehan Shipbuilding at a price of USD 99.3 m per vessel with delivery within the second quarter of 2026.
Meanwhile, we are hearing a 2009 Chinese built Suezmax has been sold at USD 42.5 m. Lastly, two modern LR2s 109K DWT 2024 built are rumored sold at USD 84.5 m each.
Source: Clarkson Platou (Hellas) ltd

Compared to previous weeks, the dry bulk market has shown increased strength.The gearless tonnage led the way with few mid aged KMXs and PMXs being sold.
On the wet side, following an exceptionally strong start of the year, sales activity moderated. However, overall sentiment remains constructive, supported by continued interest especially in the crude sector.
Dry Cargo
On the gearless segment a couple of Kamsarmaxes have been sold. The RIZE (ABT 81K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI MIPO) at circa USD 17.5m, and a 20-year-old Japanese built ship that, according to rumors, has achieved levels in the high USD 10'sm.
On the Panamax front, the GLOBAL BONANZA (ABT 75K DWT, 2011, SASEBO) sold at USD 15.3 m to Greek interests, basis surveys due. We are hearing that a 2006 LME has also been sold for USD 9.7m.
Meanwhile, the Ultramax MITSOS (ABT 63K DWT, 2013, CHENGXI) was acquired by Greek interests for USD 20.5m.
Tanker
Following the numerous VLCCs sales of the past few weeks, another vintage ship has been reported sold, namely the DHT BAUHINIA (ABT 301K DWT, 2007, DAEWOO) that fetched a price of USD 51.5m basis June-July delivery.
Source: Clarkson Platou (Hellas) ltd

Snp markets have maintained strong sentiment across sectors, building on a positive start to the year.
On the dry bulk side, the prevailing trend continues to favor larger tonnage transactions, supported by firm freight rates despite the approaching Lunar New Year, a period that is traditionally slower for market activity.
Meanwhile, the tanker market has recorded another strong week, with demand continuing to build rapidly and buyer appetite remaining robust. Numerous discussions are currently underway, and we are expecting to be able to report more sales in the coming weeks.
Dry Cargo
On the bulk carrier front, several transactions occurred across a wide range of sizes.
At the larger end, the Capesize ROBUSTO (ABT 174 DWT, 2006, SWS, SCRUBBER) was sold to Chinese interests for USD 19.5 m with delivery in Far East between April - May 2026.
In the Post Panamax segment, the JP CARETTA (ABT 88K DWT, 2008, IMABARI, SCRUBBER) was reported sold at region USD 13 m, while the Kamsarmax GASTONE (ABT 81K DWT, 2012, SUNGDONG) achieved a price of USD 17.6 m.
Within the geared segment, the Supramax SPAR CANIS (ABT 53K DWT, 2006, SHANGHAI CHENGXI) was reported sold at region USD 9 m to Chinese buyers, and the Handysize JETSTREAM (ABT 34K, 2012, SPP GOSEONG) changed hands at USD 13.5 m.
Tanker
On the tanker sector, the LR1 ATHIRI (ABT 74K DWT, 2010, SPP SACHEON) was acquired by Greek interests at USD 25 m.

Tankers and Bulkers continue to benefit from overall firm market sentiment, supporting steady levels of secondhand activity across the board. Buyers remain engaged, with transactions materializing in both larger and mid-sized segments as confidence in earnings and asset values persists.
On the dry side, Chinese interests have been particularly active in the Capesize segment. Meanwhile, the tanker market maintains solid momentum across all sectors, with strong buying appetite from Far Eastern and Greek buyers.
Dry Cargo
On the Capesize front, activity has remained firm, with several notable transactions concluded during the week. The scrubber-fitted STAR SCARLETT (ABT 175K DWT, 2014, JINHAI, SCRUBBER) was acquired by Chinese interests at around USD 36 m. Meantime, the EPIC (ABT 182K DWT, 2010, ODENSE LINDO) was sold at USD 32.5 m, and the same aged Chinese built CAPE BRAZIL (ABT 177K DWT, 2010, SWS) achieved a price of USD 31 m.
In the Handysize segment, activity was more selective, yet present. The CS CANDY (ABT 37K DWT, 2012, TIANJIN XIANGANG, ICE CLASS 1C) was sold at levels in the mid to high USD 11s m.
Tanker
On tankers, the VLCC sector witnessed another landmark transaction, as c/o Pan Ocean secured 10 scrubber-fitted VLCCs from SK Shipping, including units built between 2008 and 2013. The enbloc deal concluded at around USD 668 m and includes attached time-charter agreements back to SK Shipping.
C/o Euronav have sold the sister VLCCs ILMA & INGRID (ABT 318K DWT, 2012, HYUNDAI HI) to S. Korean interests reportedly generating a combined capital gain of USD 98.2 m. The transaction highlights the strong demand and continued liquidity in the VLCC space, with a stronger preference towards Korean-built tonnage.
Meanwhile on Suezmaxes, c/o Nordic Tankers sold the NORDIC POLLUX (ABT 150K DWT, 2003, NKK (TSU)) at USD 25 m.
The product tanker segment has also been experiencing increased activity.

Activity has moderated this week as the Lunar New Year period temporarily slows market momentum.
But despite seasonal slowdown, overall asset values continue to hold at firm levels across sectors, reflecting underlying confidence in earnings and sustained buying appetite.
With several offer deadlines scheduled for next week, activity is expected to accelerate, and we will be able to report further as the market momentum builds.
Dry Cargo
Further activity was recorded in the larger sizes, with the Capesize MICHALIS H (ABT 180K DWT, 2012, DAILAN, SCRUBBER) reported sold at USD 35.2 m, reflecting continued appetite for Capesize tonnage.
In the geared segment, the Supramax LIANSON DYNAMIC (ABT 53K DWT, 2006, CHENGXI) was reported sold at levels in xs USD 9 m.
Whilst we are hearing of a 2010 Japanese built Supramax being committed in levels close to USD 15 m.
Tanker
On the VLCC front, the scrubber fitted SINGAPORE SPIRIT (ABT 318K DWT, 2013, SWS) is reported sold at USD 84.5 m to C/O Sinokor.
Additionally, on the Aframax segment, the Korean built P. SOPHIA (ABT 105K DWT, 2009, Hyundai HI Ulsan) has changed hands achieving USD 36.65 m.
Meanwhile, in the MR space, the zinc coated CABO NEGRO II (ABT 47K DWT, 2006, SK Onishi) is reported sold at levels in the low USD 14 m range.
Source: Clarkson Platou (Hellas) ltd

Both dry bulk and tanker secondhand markets have remained active, with bulker deals particularly active.
Transactions continue to materialize, reflecting sustained buyers' appetite despite asset prices across both sectors continuing to push at higher levels, supporting overall market confidence.
Dry Cargo
On the Kamsarmax front, c/o Agricore Shipping have concluded the sale of the ASL MOON (ABT 81K DWT, 2008, MITSUI TAMANO) at USD 13.6 m to Chinese interests.
Meanwhile, after having invited offers earlier in the week, the THREE SASKIAS (ABT 80K DWT, 2014, JMU TSU) has been committed at levels of USD 26.7 m to Far Eastern interests.
In addition, the GIEWONT (ABT 79K DWT, 2010, NEW CENTURY) has been concluded at USD 11.8 m, with Chinese being rumored as the buyers.
In the Supramax segment, c/o Densay Shipping have sold the SSI ERDOGAN BEY (ABT 50K DWT, 2010, OSHIMA) at USD 15 m, basis surveys freshly passed.
Finally, in the Handysize sector, the ADVENTURE (ABT 33K DWT, 2011, WEIHAI SAMJIN) has changed hands for USD 9.5 m basis a very prompt delivery with surveys imminently due.
Tanker
On the wet side, prices have continued to strengthen, with the present week forming no exception.
The scrubber fitted Suezmax SIGRUN (ABT 156K DWT, 2013, SUMITOMO) is reported sold at USD 65 m to C/O Naftomar.

stockpiles in China have now reached a record 162 million tonnes, eclipsing the
previous peak established in 2018. Despite this surplus and generally sluggish steel
demand, prices remain resilient, hovering just below the $100/mt mark, stabilized
by the centralized procurement strategies of the China Mineral Resources Group
(CMRG). Much like its strategic management and increase of crude oil reserves,
China's continued aggressive acquisition of iron ore despite high inventories
remains an enigma; however, this activity has so far provided a significant tailwind
for the dry bulk shipping sector. While current iron ore prices may seem excessive
relative to the cooling domestic steel market, CMRG's oversight provides a
stabilizing mechanism capable of maintaining price equilibrium for both domestic
mills and global mining operators.
• Our Long-term View - The last few years have been characterized by increased
geopolitical uncertainty. Going forward, we expect such events to continue to affect
global trade and have a meaningful impact on effective vessel supply. Combined
with the potential for a multi-year cyclical rebound in China's economic activity
following the recent economic turmoil, dry bulk shipping should experience higher
volatility on top of a secular tightness driven by stable bulk commodity demand and
rather steady fleet growth.

HD Hyundai Samho said Friday it has secured a 263.2 billion won ($179 milion) order to build two oil tankers for a shipping company in Greece.
The deal covers two 157,000-deadweight-ton tankers, with deliveries scheduled by May 2029, the company said in a regulatory filing. The name of the Greece-based client was not disclosed.
HD Hyundai Samho is one of three shipbuilding affiliates under HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE), along with HD Hyundai Heavy Industries and HD Hyundai Mipo Dockyard.
HD KSOE is a sub-holding company of HD Hyundai, Korea's leading shipbuilding group.
HD KSOE aims to secure $23.31 billion worth of orders this year, up from $18.16 billion last year. Source: Korea JoongAng Daily

Another strong week in the S&P market, particularly within the dry bulk segment, where fresh benchmark sales emerged at firmer levels. A couple of flagship deals in both the Kamsarmax and Handysize sectors set the tone, highlighting the upward momentum.
Demand remains strong across the board, while the limited availability of quality tonnage continues to push asset values.
Dry Cargo
The CCS ORCHID (ABT 82K DWT, 2017, JIANGSU NEW YANGZIJIANG) has been sold via online auction, at USD 27.24 m to Greek buyers. 18 buyers bid in total, with the reserve price being USD 22.78 m.
On the Handysize front, the modern SIDER IMABARI (ABT 40K DWT, 2024, SHIMANAMI) was sold for USD 34.8 m. Meanwhile, the Japanese controlled PACIFIC HARMONY (ABT 38K DWT, 2013, IMABARI), after being inspected by more than 15 Buyers last week, eventually sold for region USD 18 m basis drydock due in May 2026. For comparison, the last sistership sold was the TBC PRIME (ABT 38K DWT, 2011 MINAMINIPPON) that fetched USD 14.1 m back in November 2025.
Tanker
Two MR sales have been recorded, with the scrubber fitted sister vessels FINNANGER (ABT 46K DWT, 2009, HYUNDAI MIPO) and FJELLANGER (ABT 46K DWT, 2010, HYUNDAI MIPO) committed enbloc to c/o Msea Tankers, achieving a combined price of mid USD 47 m.
Source: Clarkson Platou (Hellas) ltd

The S&P market remains active, with asset values in both the tanker and dry bulk sectors remaining firm.
Modern eco-design vessels are drawing particularly strong interest and achieving premium levels, while older, non-eco tonnage is also maintaining liquidity, successfully attracting buyers and securing solid prices.
Dry Cargo
In the Kamsarmax segment, after inviting offers on Monday, the MG MERCURY (ABT 85K DWT, 2016, IMABARI, BEAM 35 M) was acquired by European interests at levels in the low USD 28's m.
On the Panamax front, the BARWON (ABT 78K DWT, 2015, SASEBO, ECO ME) invited offers earlier this week, attracting interest from up to 5 buyers, and has now been reported sold for xs USD 26 m.
On the geared segment, we understand that a 2021 Japanese Ultramax was sold for region USD 37 m, whilst the Supramax FIGEAC (ABT 53K DWT, 2011, CHENGXI) was sold for a price close to USD 12 m, basis surveys promptly due. Meanwhile, the older SOMNATH (ABT 55K DWT, 2005, OSHIMA) was sold at region USD 9 m.
Tankers
The Handy MR CHRYSOPIGI (ABT 38K DWT, 2006, GUANGZHOU) was sold at USD 9 m, basis surveys promptly due.

This week, the S&P market has adopted a more cautious tone, however, a fair number of transactions have still materialized across segments. Activity appears more selective and targeted, with the market continuing to be shaped by firm price expectations from Sellers.
Dry Cargo
In the Capesize sector, Japanese owners invited offers last week for the FRONTIER GARLAND (ABT 181K DWT, 2011, IMABARI) and is now reported sold to Greek interests at USD 36.4m.
Elsewhere, the modern Kamsarmax GIA INSPIRATION (ABT 85K DWT, 2022, CSSC TIANJIN) has changed hands at around USD 33.5m, while the Panamax AGRI KINSALE (ABT 77K DWT, 2009, OSHIMA SHIPBUILDING), controlled by c/o Fortune Ocean Shipping, was sold to undisclosed buyers at levels in the low USD 15m's.
In the Ultramax segment, the JIN RUI (ABT, 63K DWT, 2014, JIANGSU HANTONG) has been sold to Chinese interests at USD 24m.
Tankers
In the Tanker space, several vessels attracted offers this week. Among them were the Korean-owned 2 x VLCCs, C. PROGRESS (ABT 313K DWT, 2012, HD HYUNDAI) and C. INNOVATOR (ABT 297K DWT, 2012, DALIAN), as well as the MR Tanker, PRO ONYX (ABT 50K DWT, 2019, HYUNDAI MIPO), which are currently under negotiations.
Additionally, in the MR segment, another sale has been concluded, this time from c/o d'Amico Tankers, who have sold their HIGH SEAS (ABT 51K DWT 2012, HYUNDAI MIPO), for levels of high USD 27 m to Greek buyers.

This week in the S&P market, Owners appeared to be adopting a more cautious, wait-and-see approach towards engaging in new deals. At the same time prices continued following the upward trend of the past months and we saw numerous transactions concluding - particularly stemming from negotiations initiated in previous weeks.
Notably, attention has remained drawn to the Dry Bulk sector: Greeks are showing continued interest in ~15-year-old Kamsarmax tonnage, confirming a healthy demand in this segment. At the same time, Asian buyers demonstrated appetite for well-priced Supramaxes.
Dry Cargo
In the Supramax sector, the PETRUS (ABT 57K DWT, 2011, STX JINGHAE) was sold for a price in the high USD 13m's, and the MERCURY OCEAN (ABT 53K DWT, 2008, IWAGI ZOSEN) achieved a price of low USD 13m from Chinese buyers - both vessels surveys due in April 26'. We are hearing as well of a 2009 55K DWT Hyundai Vinashin built Supramax being sold for USD 13.4m.
In the Handysize front, the DL OLIVE (ABT 35K DWT, 2013, SPP) was acquired by Greek interests for USD 15.3m and the ATLANTIC SPIRIT (ABT 35K DWT, 2013, NANJING) achieved a price in the mid-high 12m's. On the smaller side, the SAFI FORTUNE (ABT 28K DWT, 2009, IMABARI) sold at around USD 9.7m.
Tanker
In the wet segment, activity was particularly focused on product tankers. The Chinese-built LR1 sister vessels, PM IMPERIAL and PM MONARCH (ABT 76K DWT, 2007, DALIAN) were reported sold enbloc for xs USD 20m each.
In the MR space, the Korean-built eco-vessels of Scorpio, STI BROOKLYN and STI BLACK HAWK (ABT 50K DWT, 2015, SPP / HMD, SCRUBBER), were concluded at around USD 35m each, both fitted with scrubbers and expected for delivery in Q2.

on-week increase of the BDI. Numerous enquiries were recorded across all vessel types, with particular
focus on 15-20-year-old Panamax and Kamsarmax tonnage built in Japan, while demand for eco
bulkers remains firm amid limited availability of prompt candidates. Activity in the tanker segment has
maintained a more subdued tone, although we are aware of a fair number of ongoing negotiations.
Dry Cargo
In the Kamsarmax sector, the AVALON (ABT 81K DWT, 2011, SUNGDONG) is understood committed at
region USD 18m, whilst the older MANDY MORN (ABT 82K DWT, 2008, TSUNEISHI ZOUSHAN) was reported
sold to Chinese interests at levels circa USD 14m.
On the Panamax segment, the PRABHU YUVIKA (ABT 76K DWT, 2004, SUMITOMO) was sold at mid-high
USD 9m.
Market rumors indicate that a 2017 Chinese Ultramax is being negotiated in region USD 26/27m.
Moving to the Supramax size, the VALIANT WAVE (ABT 53K DWT, 2005, IMABARI) was committed at USD
10.5m. After inviting offers this week, we understand the SUMAQ QUEEN (ABT 51K DWT, 2017, IMABARI)
has seen interest from more than 5 buyers at mid USD 25m levels and is currently under negotiations.
We are hearing as well of a 2008 Mitsui sold for USD 14m basis very prompt delivery.

ongoing Strait of Hormuz (SOH) disruption represents a generational shift in global research@breakwaveadvisors.com
market dynamics, shifting the previous surplus into a structural deficit that will
likely persist for years. While historically high inventory levels initially cushioned the
impact, three months of continuous depletion have severely eroded this safety
margin. Consequently, global oil prices are projected to remain above $90 per
barrel absent a global recession, a threshold that will significantly elevate worldwide
inflation expectations and interest rates. As entering the summer months
accelerates this supply-demand imbalance, the resulting market strain is anticipated
to trigger widespread logistical disruptions, permanent demand destruction,
and a heavily accelerated transition toward alternative energy investments.

of staggered rates as the growth in new vessel supply shrunk while oil demand
remained elevated in line with the global economy. The recent rapid increase in
freight rates has led to significant new vessel ordering, with the orderbook now
standing at above average levels, and although in the near term such a
supply/demand misbalance is small, we expect a meaningful negative balance to
develop longer term leading to a potential downcycle.

Following the ongoing strong market momentum, this week's SnP activity has continued along the same trend.
We have recorded several sales across dry segments, with a particular focus on about 15-20-year-old larger bulk carrier tonnage. Across the space, a significant number of vessels are currently receiving offers with deadlines extending into next week. One of the main talking points of the market is a 2011-built Japanese Kamsarmax calling for offers next week, for which we understand around 10 buyers have registered interest.
Tankers values have remained very firm, despite a slight softening in rates compared to previous weeks. Tanker demand remains present but selective, while promptly available ECO-type wet tonnage remains scarce. Much attention was dawn to a 2012 Chinese-built MR2 achieving a price of close to USD 28m after calling for offers early in the week and receiving bids from a handful of buyers, the majority of which were reported Greek.
Dry Cargo
On the Capesize front, the CHIN SHAN (ABT 176K DWT, 2004, CSBC) was sold for USD 20.3m to undisclosed interests.
In the Post-Panamax segment, the modern LOWLANDS TEAL (ABT 95K DWT, 2020, OSHIMA) was sold at USD 36.5m, while the three years older sister vessel LOWLANDS DAWN (ABT 94K DWT, 2017, OSHIMA) is understood committed at excess USD 31m.
Further activity was recorded in the Kamsarmax sector, where the eco NORD POLARIS (ABT 82K DWT, 2016, TSUNEISHI CEBU) achieved low USD 28m. The scrubber-fitted XENIA (ABT 87K DWT, 2006, I.H.I. YOKOHAMA, SCRUBBER) was sold for USD 13m, while the PEDHOULAS COMMANDER (ABT 84K DWT, 2008, SANOYAS HISHINO) achieved a price of USD 14.7m. The PANAGIA FORCE (ABT 82K DWT, 2007, MITSUI) was sold at levels around USD 13.5m.

As we enter the vibrant week of Posidonia, market sentiment is on positive tune and the SnP activity remains busy across both Dry and Tanker segments.
On the Dry front we continue to observe a sustained appetite for both ECO candidates and mid-aged tonnage, with activity evident across a broad range of sizes and with the majority of sales being concentrated around non-geared vessels. Much attention was drawn to the sale of the Capesize EHIME QUEEN (ABT 181K DWT, 2016, IMABARI), which after reportedly attracting approximately 5 offers, is understood to have achieved a fixing price in the region of USD 56m. Meantime, we are observing a number of enquiries for around 15-year-old built Supramaxes as reflected by rumors of a 2012 Dolphin 57 with surveys passed being committed for levels in the USD mid 15m. At the same time, demand for around 15-to-20-year-old Panamax and Kamsarmaxes remains steady.
On the Tanker side, buyers are continuing to show appetite for ECO tonnage despite the small decline in rates. Activity has been primarily concentrated around MR and Aframax / LR2 candidates, although notable interest is evident across all segments.
Dry Cargo
On the Capesize front, the Japanese built scrubber fitted EHIME QUEEN (ABT 181K DWT, 2016, IMABARI, SCRUBBER) was sold at region USD 56m to Chinese buyers.
Meanwhile, in the Kamsarmax space, the KEY HUNTER (ABT 82K DWT, 2011, TSUNEISHI) was acquired by Greek interests at a price in the region of USD 21m.
On the Ultramax front, the Chinese built sister vessels TIAN MU SHAN and YAN DANG SHAN (ABT 63K DWT, 2017, SHUNTIAN SB (JIANGSU)) were sold enbloc this week via the GSE auction platform at USD 52.32m by clients of CDB Leasing to Singaporean based interests.
Lastly, on the Handysize segment, the ASAHI OCEAN (ABT 32K DWT, 2013, HAKODATE DOCK) was reported sold at USD 15.2m to undisclosed interests.
Tanker

What a week! One of the biggest and busiest Posidonia events ever. With the majority of shipping sectors enjoying healthy market conditions,the global maritime community gathered in Athens for a week of meetings, networking, celebrations, and strategic discussions. The overall sentiment was positive, with market participants expressing optimism that supportive fundamentals will continue to underpin freight markets in the months ahead.
At the same time, there remains a degree of caution regarding ongoing geopolitical developments in the Middle East and their potential implications for global trade flows, energy markets, and overall economic stability.
S&P demand and activity remain robust, with the shortage of modern eco-design bulkers and tankers still very evident. One might have expected more owners to take advantage of current asset values and bring additional tonnage to the market; however, many continue to prefer retaining exposure to what they believe could be a prolonged period of healthy earnings.
Looking ahead, the industry appears to be entering the second half of the year with a constructive outlook. While macroeconomic and geopolitical risks cannot be ignored, the prevailing mood at Posidonia suggested that most market participants remain confident in the resilience of shipping markets and the opportunities that lie ahead.
Dry Cargo
In the Kamsarmax sector, Chinese Buyers have emerged behind the DIMITRIS A (ABT 83K DWT, 2008, TSUNEISHI ZHOUSHAN), which was sold for USD 14.8m.
On the Supramax front, the AE MARS (ABT 53K DWT, 2006, SINOPACIFIC DAYANG) was sold via auction at xs USD 9m to Chinese interests.
Tanker
Although no new tanker sales can be reported, several negotiations are understood to be ongoing this week.

positive, with market participants expressing optimism that supportive fundamentals will continue to
underpin freight markets in the months ahead.
At the same time, there remains a degree of caution regarding ongoing geopolitical developments in
the Middle East and their potential implications for global trade flows, energy markets, and overall
economic stability.
S&P demand and activity remain robust, with the shortage of modern eco-design bulkers and tankers
still very evident. One might have expected more owners to take advantage of current asset values
and bring additional tonnage to the market; however, many continue to prefer retaining exposure to
what they believe could be a prolonged period of healthy earnings.
Looking ahead, the industry appears to be entering the second half of the year with a constructive
outlook. While macroeconomic and geopolitical risks cannot be ignored, the prevailing mood at
Posidonia suggested that most market participants remain confident in the resilience of shipping
markets and the opportunities that lie ahead.

Although no new tanker sales can be reported, several negotiations are understood to be ongoing this

text:
The US-Iran ceasefire has not yet changed much on the water, while the impact of the signing of the Memorandum of Agreement betweenthe US and Iran on the Hormuz chokepoint remains to be seen. For now, uncertainty surrounding transit through the Strait persists, with the number of monitored transits still well below pre-conflict levels.
In dry bulk, rates softened with the recording a week-on-week decline of approximately 7.3%. On tankers, in contrast to the rate easing seen in previous weeks, a slight increase was observed this week, particularly across the larger tanker segments.
Overall, we observed healthy S&P activity this week in both the Dry and Wet markets, despite fluctuations in freight rates. As many had anticipated, the U.S.-Iran ceasefire has failed to hold, with renewed hostilities threatening to underminethe fragile optimism that the traffic in the Straits of Hormuz will be fully restored sooner than later.
The latest developments have reinforced concerns that geopolitical risks remain elevated and continue to influence the decisions of Buyers and Sellers in all segments.
On the commodity side, coal demand in the Far East is expected to strengthen, with Vietnam projected to reach record coal imports in 2026.
This growth is driven by government plans to expand the country's power generation capacity through alternative energy sources, including coal.
More broadly, this reflects a trend that other energy-import-dependent countries may also follow if tensions in the Middle East persist and continue to disrupt global energy supply routes, suggesting an optimistic landscape for seaborne trade in the short-and-medium-term.
These developments have been reflected in this week's Drybulk market, where Capesize experienced a strong week, with the Baltic Capesize Index closing today at 4,655, representing a 13.5% week-on-week increase.
In Tankers, VLCC activity in the Middle East has strengthened as well, further bolstered by Saudi Aramco's aggressive price cuts for its August crude export program and the UAE's record-high crude oil production in June following its exit from the OPEC.
Fixture volumes have increased as a result, although it remains uncertain whether fixtures from inside the Strait of Hormuz will conclude.
Dry Cargo
Activity in the Ultramax market saw the HAATO (ABT 61,472 DWT, 2011, SHIN KASADO DOCK, C:4X30.5T) committed to C/O ADNOC at USD 23.5m, with the deal concluded basis freshly passed surveys.
Elsewhere, in the Supramax sector EVEREST (ABT 57,480 DWT, 2012, STX SB (JINHAE), C:4X30T) reportedly sold for a price in the low USD 16m's.
Additionally, the modern Handysize JNS PHOENIX (ABT 40,552 DWT, 2025 JIANGMEN NANYANG, C:4X30T) has been committed at a price of excess USD 34m after calling for offers.

Nearing the end of the second week after the interim peace deal between Iran and United States began to break down, and amid renewed attackson vessels in the MEG, we've now reached the lowest daily total tonnage transit number through the SoH at 0.2m GT on Monday, amounting to >95% below typical daily volumes. Following the temporary easing of sanctions, Iran increased crude exports during the brief truce, leading to a rise in floating oil supplies. However, crude sales have remained subdued as China's independent refiners have opted for cheaper cargo from Iraq, the UAE, and Qatar.
At the same time, energy shipping markets remain at very elevated levels across all segments as reflected on S&P asset prices.
This week saw healthy ordering activity spread across multiple shipping segments, including Suezmax tankers, MR tankers, LNG carriers, and VLGCs. Meanwhile, benchmark newbuild prices in the tanker market have continued climbing on the back of robust demand for new vessels - VLCCs NB prices are now 2% higher since the start of the year, Suezmaxes are up 4%, and MRs have risen by 5%.
In the secondhand market, the dry bulk sector once again accounted for the majority of transaction activity this week, with prominent demand observed for geared tonnage ranging from larger Handysize up to Ultramax bulk carriers. For comparison purposes in ECO Ultramaxes, although not identically designed, BLUE AKIHABARA (ABT 61,630 DWT, 2014, NANTONG COSCO KHI (NACKS), CR:4X30T) achieved a price of excess USD 25m this week, when in May the two-year-younger sister-vessels HUAYANG ROSE and HUAYANG LILY (ABT 63,562 DWT, 2016, CHINA SHIPPING INDUSTRY (JIANGSU), CR:4X30) were understood to have been concluded at xs USD 25m each basis an enbloc sale.

With the conflict in the Middle East Gulf escalating further, this week's incidents mark the first Houthi attacks on vessels within the Red Seain over 6 months, and more specifically on two Saudi-linked tankers, a 2003 built LR2 and a 2007 built VLCC. Moreover, a review of the crude tankers and VLGCs that have departed Yanbu recently shows that only about half of the vessels are taking the risk of exiting the Red Sea through the Gulf of Aden or the Suez Canal, a sign which is consistent with the overall uncertainty in the region.
Amid the escalated tensions at the Strait of Hormuz, two scenarios can be pointed out to have bolstered the oil market: If all current Yanbu crude exports destined for Asia were rerouted via the Suez Canal and then through Cape of Good Hope, global crude tonne-mile demand could theoretically increase. Under an alternative scenario in which Yanbu exports are redirected primarily to Europe, displacing U.S.- to-Europe crude flows, with those U.S. volumes instead moving to Asia, global crude tonne-mile demand could increase as well.
The S&P wet market has in turn been once again positively influenced by the increased freight demand, with the observed tanker appetite being reflected in enquiry count, and the increasing asset prices. Out of all enquiries, 15-20-year-old VLCCs, Suezmaxes and Aframaxes stand out, while product tankers spanning a wide age range are also receiving interest. There is a number of modern eco MR2s that are also receiving attention and are being negotiated at firm levels.
On the dry side, freight market has strengthened, driven by a sharp increase in Capesize earnings, supporting stronger demand and sentiment in the larger vessel segment. At the same time, demand remains healthy across all vessel sizes, with the geared segment, particularly Ultramax and Supramax vessels, attracting the majority of the attention. For comparison, we are hearing of a 53K 2011 Chinese Supramax being sold in the low USD 15m's, whilst four months ago, a same aged sister vessel achieved a price of USD 12m, basis surveys due delivery.

Events in the Middle East are continuing to shape shipping dynamics. With disruptions now affecting Saudi Arabia's two key export routes-the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb-the effective voyage duration for Middle Eastern crude destined for Asia has increased by approximately one month and tanker earnings have now climbed at a weighted average of USD 75,000/ day, highest number since early May. Market outlook appears to be overall positive, supported by fundamentals such as the continued growth in long-haul exports, increasing Venezuelan exports now carried on "mainstream" tankers, and oil restocking margins.
S&P tanker activity was further bolstered this week, with several fairly modern VLCCs understood to have been transacted to Middle Eastern interests at firm price levels, supporting sentiment across the rest of the tanker market. We also understand that several eco MR2s ranging from circa 10-year-old units up to resales are currently under firm negotiations. Furthermore, buying appetite continues to extend also on the older units, within the 15-20-year-old range - in which we still monitor a number of buyers, mostly from the Middle East and Far East markets, being on the look-out for MRs & LR1s as well as crude takers, more specifically on Aframaxes & Suezmaxes.
Dry market has held to a robust first half of the year, underpinned by strong iron ore exports from Australia and Brazil, alongside resilient Chinese import demand despite elevated inventories and softer domestic steel production. Additional support has come from steady minor bulk trade and healthy Atlantic grain export volumes.
Looking ahead, the Capesize segment is expected to continue outperforming the smaller size classes, driven by sustained growth in long-haul Atlantic iron ore exports and favorable ton-mile demand. In terms of activity, market sources indicated a number of approximately 15-year-old Korean- and Japanese-built Kamsarmax units as being currently in advanced negotiations, while the focus of Dry Tonnage buyers seems to be in the 15-20-years-old Supramax-Ultramax segment, driven by Far Eastern market players

• Oil Prices Remain Sensitive to Hormuz Developments - Crude oil prices have
once again fluctuated in response to developments surrounding the Strait of
Hormuz, defying ongoing structural supply deficits and persistent market
Breakwave Advisors Research
uncertainty. Thus far, decelerating demand across Asia, particularly from China, has research@breakwaveadvisors.com

tightening balances in the coming months. Consequently, we anticipate
heightened volatility as oil prices gradually establish a higher baseline.

remained elevated in line with the global economy. The recent rapid increase in
freight rates has led to significant new vessel ordering, with the orderbook now
standing at well above average levels, and although in the near term such a
supply/demand misbalance is small, we expect a meaningful negative balance to
develop longer term leading to an industry downcycle.
